//: Single-field index exemptions for run geometry.
Firestore indexes every field of every document by default, and for an
array of maps that means one index entry per element. A 4,000-point track
wrote 4,000 index entries, a fourteen-year history wrote millions, and the
index cost more storage than the documents it pointed at. Every write had
to build all of them, which is the part an import feels as slowness.
Nothing in this app queries, orders by or filters on an individual track
point, a sample or a country inside a route. They are read whole, with the
document. So the index buys nothing and is turned off for those fields.
New geometry is written as an encoded polyline string on `track`, which is
indexed once however long it is; `track.points` is exempted anyway because
a 28 kB string in an index is pure waste.
`coordinates` and `samples` remain here because documents written before
the polyline change still carry them and are never migrated.
